name: Galaxy-TS-TW
title: Galaxy
description: A full-screen realistic starfield of tiny white, pink and blue stars with glowing cross flares. The field drifts and twinkles slowly, and moving the pointer bends nearby stars into radial streaks.
use: You want a calm, deep-space backdrop for a dark hero, with a subtle pointer reaction to reward exploring.
avoid: The stars are small and sparse, so on a bright screen they nearly disappear, and the motion never stops.
a11y: The starfield animates forever and ignores reduced-motion; the pointer warp has no keyboard or touch path. (keyboard: n-a, labels: n-a, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A near-black sky packed with hundreds of small stars in white, pink and cold blue, a few bright ones carrying thin cross-shaped flares and soft halos. Larger glows scatter across the field like distant clusters, and the background stays very dark.
behaves: The stars drift, twinkle and rotate slowly in parallax layers at different depths. Moving the cursor repels the nearby stars so they stretch into radial streaks, then the field relaxes when the pointer leaves.
customise: Props set focal point, rotation, star speed, density, hue, animation toggle, speed, mouse interaction and repulsion, glow, saturation, twinkle, rotation speed and transparency.
weight: heavy: A full-screen WebGL shader renders four star layers with 3x3 neighbourhoods every frame.
issues: The starfield is very dark and sparse, so on a bright display the stars almost vanish.
It ignores reduced-motion and never stops or pauses.
polishWhy: Believable starfield with convincing flares and parallax; the cursor warp is a little dramatic.
